findings.title: Every functional requirement has a corresponding implementation and verification task
findings.description: All FRs are covered: empty/scaffold-only and brownfield outcomes (Task 12 fixtures 1–3), shallow clone (Task 12.4 + Task 5T + Task 15.2), concept-only + code (Task 12.6), planned project with no walk (Task 12.7 + the `measureSourceVolume` spy in Task 9T), monorepo folder scoping and root CI (Task 12.5 + Task 5T), `in_progress` resume (Task 12.8), overrides including invalid-value rejection (Task 12.9 + Task 1T), `--phase 2`/explicit instruction (Task 12.10–11 + Task 9T), `template_preview` read-only (Task 12.13 + Task 11), and missing profile/prompt with no concept fallback (Task 9T + Task 10T + Task 12.12 + Task 15.4). No success criterion is left without a task.

findings.title: Technical, integration and walkthrough requirements are fully mapped
findings.description: Each mandated unit-test area has a task (Task 3T, 4T, 5T, 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T), as do the integration fixtures (Task 12), CLI/MCP parity (Task 13), build/typecheck/lint and caller updates (Task 11, Task 15), and the manual walkthrough steps 1–5 (Task 15). The future-slice integration points are honored: the squadron bullet is isolated in `renderSquadronFact()` (Task 8) and state is exported through `adoption/` (Tasks 2, 7, 9), so 262/263/264 need not touch selection logic.

findings.title: Sequence, test-with pairing and commit points are sound
findings.description: Dependencies are respected: `adoptionOutcome.ts` is seeded with the threshold in Task 3 and expanded in Task 7; the renderer (Task 8) and resolver (Task 9) follow the outcome; integrator/pipeline wiring (Tasks 10–11) follows the resolver; integration/parity (Tasks 12–13) follow the wiring. No circular dependencies. Test tasks immediately follow their implementations throughout. Commit markers sit after completed-and-tested groups (2C, 3C, 5C, 6C, 8C, 9C, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15C) — neither after every task nor only at the end.

findings.title: Implementation-dependent instructions are accurate against the current code
findings.description: `PHASE_STRINGS[2]`/`ARCHITECTURE_PHASE` and the legacy `phase 1: concept` alias exist in `projectSchema.ts`; `gitExec(args, cwd, opts)` produces `timed out after 5s` for a 5000 ms bound; `MIN_GUIDE_VERSION = '0.22.2'` and `PROMPT_FILE_RELATIVE_PATH` resolve as described; all named test files and the `test-project` fixture exist; and every `createContextPipeline(` caller (CLI `build.ts`, MCP `contextTools.ts`, and the enumerated tests) is accounted for by Task 11, with `packages/electron/out/` correctly excluded.

findings.title: No load test or extra timing test is needed, and the file correctly omits one
findings.description: D2's "under one second" target is explicitly bounded by the cap tests in Task 3T ("tests assert the caps, not timings"), and the `tests/load/` tier cited in the Context Summary is a Python-rule artifact that does not apply to this TypeScript repo. This is correctly reasoned; no load-test task or CI gating task is warranted here.

structured_findings.summary: Every functional requirement has a corresponding implementation and verification task
Technical, integration and walkthrough requirements are fully mapped
Sequence, test-with pairing and commit points are sound
Implementation-dependent instructions are accurate against the current code
No load test or extra timing test is needed, and the file correctly omits one
